subject: math
title: Grade 7 Volume of Prisms and Cylinders
seo_title: Grade 7 Volume of Prisms and Cylinders Worksheets: Free Math Practice with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Volume of rectangular prisms and cylinders
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 math worksheets on volume for the BC curriculum: counting cubes, V = l × w × h, area of base × height, cylinders with V = πr²h (π ≈ 3.14), and capacity in mL and L with fish tanks, juice cans and water tanks. 100 questions with an answer key, good FSA numeracy practice.
key_big: Volume = area of base × height. Rectangular prism: V = l × w × h. Cylinder: V = π × r² × h.
key_sub: Use the radius, not the diameter, and r² means r × r. Volume is in cubic units (cm³, m³), and 1 cm³ holds 1 mL.
body_html:
What volume means

Volume is the amount of space inside a solid. A cube with 1 cm edges has a volume of 1 cm³ (one cubic centimetre). To find a volume, count how many of these cubes fill the solid.

Rectangular prisms

V = l × w × h. The base l × w tells you how many cubes are in one layer, and h tells you how many layers.

Any prism: area of base × height

Every prism is a stack of layers shaped like its base, so V = area of base × height. Find the area of the base first, then multiply.

Cylinders

A cylinder is like a prism with a circle for a base. The area of the circle is π × r², so V = π × r² × h. Use π ≈ 3.14. The radius r goes from the centre to the edge; it is half the diameter.

Example 1

A can has a diameter of 8 cm and a height of 10 cm. What is its volume?

r = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm. V = 3.14 × 4 × 4 × 10 = 50.24 × 10.

Answer: 502.4 cm³

Volume and capacity

Capacity is how much a container can hold. 1 cm³ holds exactly 1 mL.

VolumeCapacity
1 cm³1 mL
1000 cm³ (a 10 cm cube)1 L
1 m³1000 L
Example 2

A fish tank is 60 cm × 30 cm × 40 cm. How many litres does it hold?

V = 60 × 30 × 40 = 72 000 cm³ = 72 000 mL. Divide by 1000.

Answer: 72 L

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the edges: 6 + 4 + 5 = 15Multiply them: 6 × 4 × 5 = 120
Stopping at the base: 6 × 4 = 24Multiply by the height too
Using the diameter as rHalve the diameter first: d = 8, r = 4
r² as r × 2r² = r × r: 4² = 16, not 8
Forgetting ½ for a triangle baseTriangle area = ½ × b × h
Writing cm² for a volumeVolume is in cubic units: cm³, m³

faq.q: How do you find the volume of a cylinder in Grade 7?
faq.a: Find the area of the circular base with π × r × r (π ≈ 3.14), then multiply by the height. For r = 3 cm and h = 10 cm: 3.14 × 9 × 10 = 282.6 cm³.

faq.q: What volume topics are in the BC Grade 7 math curriculum?
faq.a: The BC Grade 7 curriculum includes the volume of rectangular prisms and cylinders. Students connect volume to area of base × height and work with cm³, m³, mL and L.

faq.q: What is the difference between volume and capacity?
faq.a: Volume is the space a solid takes up, in cubic units like cm³. Capacity is how much a container holds, in mL or L, and 1 cm³ = 1 mL.

faq.q: Do these volume worksheets help with the Grade 7 FSA?
faq.a: Yes. The Grade 7 FSA includes numeracy, where students use math to solve problems. Finding how much a tank, can or box holds is good practice for that kind of problem.

items.q: A cube has edges that are 1 cm long. What is its volume?
items.e: A cube with 1 cm edges is the unit for volume: 1 cm³ (one cubic centimetre). 1 cm² is the area of one face, and 1 cm is the length of one edge.

items.q: Each small cube is 1 cm³. What is the volume of this prism?
items.e: Each layer has 2 rows of 2 cubes = 4 cubes. There are 3 layers: 4 × 3 = 12 cm³. Count the hidden cubes, too: only 10 cubes show a face.

items.q: Each small cube is 1 cm³. What is the volume of this prism?
items.e: Each layer has 3 rows of 3 cubes = 9 cubes. There are 2 layers: 9 × 2 = 18 cm³. Count the hidden cubes, too: only 14 cubes show a face.

items.q: Each small cube is 1 cm³. What is the volume of this prism?
items.e: Each layer has 2 rows of 5 cubes = 10 cubes. There are 2 layers: 10 × 2 = 20 cm³. Count the hidden cubes, too: only 16 cubes show a face.

items.q: Each small cube is 1 cm³. What is the volume of this prism?
items.e: Each layer has 2 rows of 3 cubes = 6 cubes. There are 3 layers: 6 × 3 = 18 cm³. Count the hidden cubes, too: only 14 cubes show a face.

items.q: Each small cube is 1 cm³. What is the volume of this prism?
items.e: Each layer has 2 rows of 2 cubes = 4 cubes. There are 2 layers: 4 × 2 = 8 cm³. Count the hidden cubes, too: only 7 cubes show a face.

items.q: Each small cube is 1 cm³. What is the volume of this prism?
items.e: Each layer has 3 rows of 3 cubes = 9 cubes. There are 3 layers: 9 × 3 = 27 cm³. Count the hidden cubes, too: only 19 cubes show a face.

items.q: Each small cube is 1 cm³. What is the volume of this prism?
items.e: Each layer has 2 rows of 3 cubes = 6 cubes. There are 2 layers: 6 × 2 = 12 cm³. Count the hidden cubes, too: only 10 cubes show a face.

items.q: How many centimetre cubes are in the bottom layer of this prism?
items.e: The bottom layer is 5 cubes across and 2 cubes deep: 5 × 2 = 10 cubes. The front face shows 5 × 4 = 20 cubes, but that is not a layer.

items.q: How many centimetre cubes are in the bottom layer of this prism?
items.e: The bottom layer is 5 cubes across and 3 cubes deep: 5 × 3 = 15 cubes. The front face shows 5 × 2 = 10 cubes, but that is not a layer.

items.q: How many centimetre cubes are in the bottom layer of this prism?
items.e: The bottom layer is 5 cubes across and 4 cubes deep: 5 × 4 = 20 cubes. The front face shows 5 × 2 = 10 cubes, but that is not a layer.

items.q: How many centimetre cubes are in the bottom layer of this prism?
items.e: The bottom layer is 4 cubes across and 3 cubes deep: 4 × 3 = 12 cubes. The front face shows 4 × 4 = 16 cubes, but that is not a layer.

items.q: The layers of this prism are pulled apart. Each cube is 1 cm³. What is the volume of the whole prism?
items.e: One layer: 3 × 2 = 6 cubes. 4 layers: 6 × 4 = 24 cm³.

items.q: The layers of this prism are pulled apart. Each cube is 1 cm³. What is the volume of the whole prism?
items.e: One layer: 5 × 3 = 15 cubes. 4 layers: 15 × 4 = 60 cm³.

items.q: The layers of this prism are pulled apart. Each cube is 1 cm³. What is the volume of the whole prism?
items.e: One layer: 3 × 3 = 9 cubes. 4 layers: 9 × 4 = 36 cm³.

items.q: The layers of this prism are pulled apart. Each cube is 1 cm³. What is the volume of the whole prism?
items.e: One layer: 4 × 2 = 8 cubes. 4 layers: 8 × 4 = 32 cm³.

items.q: The bottom layer of a box holds 6 rows of 4 centimetre cubes. The box holds 5 layers. What is the volume of the box?
items.e: One layer: 6 × 4 = 24 cubes. 5 layers: 24 × 5 = 120 cm³.

items.q: The bottom layer of a tray holds 8 rows of 5 centimetre cubes. The tray holds 3 layers. What is the volume of the tray?
items.e: One layer: 8 × 5 = 40 cubes. 3 layers: 40 × 3 = 120 cm³.

items.q: How many 1 cm cubes fit in a box that is 10 cm long, 6 cm wide and 4 cm high?
items.e: One layer on the bottom: 10 × 6 = 60 cubes. The box is 4 cm high, so 4 layers: 60 × 4 = 240 cubes. (20 adds the edges, 60 is only one layer, and 64 adds the height to one layer.)

items.q: A box holds 60 centimetre cubes in each layer. It holds 420 cubes in all. How many layers are there?
items.e: Cubes in one layer × number of layers = total, so 60 × ? = 420. 420 ÷ 60 = 7 layers. (360 subtracts and 480 adds.)

sets.title: Rectangular prisms: V = l × w × h

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 13 × 8 × 5 = 104 × 5 = 520 cm³. Multiply all three edges (do not add them), and write cubic units.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 6 × 5 × 2 = 30 × 2 = 60 cm³. Multiply all three edges (do not add them), and write cubic units.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 11 × 7 × 2 = 77 × 2 = 154 cm³. Multiply all three edges (do not add them), and write cubic units.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 6 × 4 × 2 = 24 × 2 = 48 m³. Multiply all three edges (do not add them), and write cubic units.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 15 × 5 × 9 = 75 × 9 = 675 cm³. Multiply all three edges (do not add them), and write cubic units.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 11 × 2 × 3 = 22 × 3 = 66 cm³. Multiply all three edges (do not add them), and write cubic units.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 6 × 3 × 2 = 18 × 2 = 36 m³. Multiply all three edges (do not add them), and write cubic units.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = l × w × h = 5 × 3 × 12 = 15 × 12 = 180 cm³. Multiply all three edges (do not add them), and write cubic units.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = 2.5 × 4 × 6 = 10 × 6 = 60 cm³. Count the decimal places to check: the answer is not 600 cm³.

items.q: What is the volume of this rectangular prism?
items.e: V = 1.5 × 2 × 0.8 = 3 × 0.8 = 2.4 m³. Count the decimal places to check: the answer is not 24 m³.

items.q: A rectangular prism is 3.2 cm long, 5 cm wide and 10 cm high. What is its volume?
items.e: V = 3.2 × 5 × 10 = 16 × 10 = 160 cm³. Count the decimal places to check: the answer is not 1600 cm³.

items.q: A rectangular prism is 0.5 m long, 0.4 m wide and 0.3 m high. What is its volume?
items.e: V = 0.5 × 0.4 × 0.3 = 0.2 × 0.3 = 0.06 m³. Check the decimal places: 0.5 × 0.4 = 0.2, and 0.2 × 0.3 = 0.06 (3 decimal places in all, 0.060).

items.q: A cube has edges that are 5 cm long. What is its volume?
items.e: All the edges of a cube are equal, so V = 5 × 5 × 5 = 25 × 5 = 125 cm³. 5 × 3 = 15 is not the volume.

items.q: A cube has edges that are 8 cm long. What is its volume?
items.e: All the edges of a cube are equal, so V = 8 × 8 × 8 = 64 × 8 = 512 cm³. 8 × 3 = 24 is not the volume.

items.q: A cube has edges that are 1.5 cm long. What is its volume?
items.e: All the edges of a cube are equal, so V = 1.5 × 1.5 × 1.5 = 2.25 × 1.5 = 3.375 cm³. 1.5 × 3 = 4.5 is not the volume.

items.q: A box is 6 cm long, 4 cm wide and 3 cm high. Which expression gives its volume?
items.e: Volume = length × width × height = 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 cm³. 6 × 4 is only the area of the base.

items.q: A shipping crate is 12 m long, 5 m wide and 2.5 m high. Which expression gives its volume?
items.e: Length × width × height = 12 × 5 × 2.5 = 60 × 2.5 = 150 m³. (12 + 5) × 2.5 adds two edges first.

items.q: A rectangular prism has a volume of 240 cm³. It is 10 cm long and 4 cm wide. How high is it?
A rectangular prism has a volume of 360 cm³. It is 12 cm long and 5 cm high. How wide is it?
A rectangular prism has a volume of 36 m³. It is 4 m long and 2.5 m wide. How high is it?
The base of a prism has an area of 24 cm². The prism is 5 cm high. What is its volume?
items.e: V = area of base × height = 24 × 5 = 120 cm³. (Adding gives 29, which is not a volume.)

items.q: The base of a prism has an area of 45 cm². The prism is 12 cm high. What is its volume?
items.e: V = area of base × height = 45 × 12 = 540 cm³. (Adding gives 57, which is not a volume.)

items.q: The base of a prism has an area of 12.5 cm². The prism is 8 cm high. What is its volume?
items.e: V = area of base × height = 12.5 × 8 = 100 cm³. (Adding gives 20.5, which is not a volume.)

items.q: The base of a prism has an area of 36 cm². The prism is 7.5 cm high. What is its volume?
items.e: V = area of base × height = 36 × 7.5 = 270 cm³. (Adding gives 43.5, which is not a volume.)

items.q: The ends of this prism are right triangles. What is its volume?
items.e: Base (the triangle): ½ × 6 × 4 = 12 cm². V = 12 × 10 = 120 cm³. Do not forget the ½: 6 × 4 × 10 = 240 is a whole box, twice too big.

items.q: The ends of this prism are right triangles. What is its volume?
items.e: Base (the triangle): ½ × 8 × 5 = 20 cm². V = 20 × 12 = 240 cm³. Do not forget the ½: 8 × 5 × 12 = 480 is a whole box, twice too big.

items.q: The ends of this prism are right triangles. What is its volume?
items.e: Base (the triangle): ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 cm². V = 30 × 15 = 450 cm³. Do not forget the ½: 10 × 6 × 15 = 900 is a whole box, twice too big.

items.q: The ends of this prism are right triangles. What is its volume?
items.e: Base (the triangle): ½ × 5 × 4 = 10 cm². V = 10 × 9 = 90 cm³. Do not forget the ½: 5 × 4 × 9 = 180 is a whole box, twice too big.

items.q: A tent is shaped like a triangular prism. Each end is a triangle with a base of 2.4 m and a height of 1.5 m. The tent is 3 m long. What is the volume of the tent?
items.e: Base: ½ × 2.4 × 1.5 = 1.8 m². V = 1.8 × 3 = 5.4 m³. Without the ½ you get 10.8, twice too big.

items.q: A chocolate box is a triangular prism. Each end is a triangle with a base of 4 cm and a height of 3.5 cm. The box is 20 cm long. What is its volume?
items.e: Base: ½ × 4 × 3.5 = 7 cm². V = 7 × 20 = 140 cm³. Without the ½ you get 280, twice too big.

items.q: A wooden ramp for a skateboard park is a triangular prism. Each side of the ramp is a triangle with a base of 120 cm and a height of 30 cm. The ramp is 80 cm wide. What is its volume?
items.e: Base: ½ × 120 × 30 = 1800 cm². V = 1800 × 80 = 144 000 cm³. Without the ½ you get 288 000, twice too big.

items.q: A prism has a base shaped like a parallelogram. The parallelogram has a base of 8 cm, a slanted side of 6 cm and a height of 5 cm. The prism is 12 cm long. What is its volume?
items.e: Area of the parallelogram = base × height = 8 × 5 = 40 cm² (use the height, not the slanted side). V = 40 × 12 = 480 cm³. 8 × 6 × 12 = 576 uses the slanted side.

items.q: The base of a prism is a trapezoid with parallel sides of 4 cm and 6 cm and a height of 3 cm. The prism is 10 cm long. What is its volume?
items.e: Area of the trapezoid = (4 + 6) ÷ 2 × 3 = 15 cm². V = 15 × 10 = 150 cm³. Forgetting to divide by 2 gives 300.

items.q: A box is 8 cm long, 5 cm wide and 3 cm high. Mei turns it so that it stands on its 5 cm × 3 cm face. What is its volume now?
items.e: Turning a box does not change the space inside it. Base 5 × 3 = 15 cm², height 8 cm: 15 × 8 = 120 cm³, the same as 8 × 5 × 3.

items.q: A prism has a volume of 360 cm³. The area of its base is 45 cm². What is its height?
items.e: V = area of base × h, so 45 × h = 360. h = 360 ÷ 45 = 8 cm.

items.q: A prism has a volume of 150 cm³. The area of its base is 25 cm². What is its height?
items.e: V = area of base × h, so 25 × h = 150. h = 150 ÷ 25 = 6 cm. The base area is already given, so do not halve or double anything.

items.q: A prism has a volume of 84 m³. The area of its base is 24 m². What is its height?
items.e: V = area of base × h, so 24 × h = 84. h = 84 ÷ 24 = 3.5 m.

items.q: Which formula gives the volume of any prism?
items.e: Every prism is a stack of layers the same shape as its base. V = area of base × height. For a box, the base area is l × w, so V = l × w × h.

items.q: A prism has a base area of 30 cm² and a height of 4 cm. The height changes to 8 cm and the base stays the same. What is the new volume?
items.e: Old volume: 30 × 4 = 120 cm³. New volume: 30 × 8 = 240 cm³. Doubling the height doubles the volume (not 4 times).

items.q: A cylinder has a base area of 28.26 cm² and a height of 10 cm. What is its volume?
items.e: A cylinder is like a prism with a circle for a base: V = area of base × height = 28.26 × 10 = 282.6 cm³. Multiplying by 10 moves the decimal point one place, not two.

items.q: A cylinder has a radius of 3 cm. What is the area of its circular base? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
A can has a diameter of 10 cm. What is the area of its circular base? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: r is half the diameter: 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm. Area = 3.14 × 5 × 5 = 3.14 × 25 = 78.5 cm². 314 uses the diameter as r, and 31.4 is the circumference.

items.e: 6 cm goes all the way across the top, so it is the diameter. r = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm. V = 3.14 × 3 × 3 × 5 = 28.26 × 5 = 141.3 cm³. Using 6 as r gives 565.2, 4 times too big.

items.q: What is the volume of this cylinder? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: 8 cm goes all the way across the top, so it is the diameter. r = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm. V = 3.14 × 4 × 4 × 10 = 50.24 × 10 = 502.4 cm³. Using 8 as r gives 2009.6, 4 times too big.

items.q: What is the volume of this cylinder? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: 10 cm goes all the way across the top, so it is the diameter. r = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm. V = 3.14 × 5 × 5 × 4 = 78.5 × 4 = 314 cm³. Using 10 as r gives 1256, 4 times too big.

items.q: What is the volume of this cylinder? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: 12 cm goes all the way across the top, so it is the diameter. r = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm. V = 3.14 × 6 × 6 × 5 = 113.04 × 5 = 565.2 cm³. Using 12 as r gives 2260.8, 4 times too big.

items.q: What is the volume of this cylinder? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: 14 cm goes all the way across the top, so it is the diameter. r = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 cm. V = 3.14 × 7 × 7 × 2 = 153.86 × 2 = 307.72 cm³. Using 14 as r gives 1230.88, 4 times too big.

items.q: A cylinder has a radius of 4 cm and a height of 10 cm. What is its volume? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
A cylinder has a radius of 1.5 cm and a height of 8 cm. What is its volume? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
A cylinder has a radius of 10 cm and a height of 2.5 cm. What is its volume? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
A cylinder has a volume of 471 cm³ and a radius of 5 cm. What is its height? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: Area of the base: 3.14 × 5 × 5 = 78.5 cm². Then 78.5 × h = 471, so h = 471 ÷ 78.5 = 6 cm.

items.q: A cylinder has a volume of 1130.4 cm³ and a radius of 6 cm. What is its height? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
A small box has a volume of 250 cm³. How many millilitres of water can it hold?
items.e: 1 cm³ holds exactly 1 mL. So 250 cm³ = 250 mL.

items.q: A cube-shaped container is 10 cm × 10 cm × 10 cm inside. How much water does it hold when full?
items.e: V = 10 × 10 × 10 = 1000 cm³ = 1000 mL = 1 L. (10 × 10 = 100 is only the base, and 30 adds the edges.)

items.q: A jug has a volume of 3500 cm³. How many litres does it hold?
A water tank holds 2 m³. How many litres is that?
items.e: 1 m³ = 100 cm × 100 cm × 100 cm = 1 000 000 cm³ = 1000 L. So 2 m³ = 2000 L. (2 000 000 is the number of mL, not L.)

items.q: Liam’s fish tank is 60 cm long, 30 cm wide and 40 cm high. How many litres does it hold when full?
Liam fills the same fish tank (60 cm long, 30 cm wide, 40 cm high) only up to 35 cm. How much water is in it?
items.e: Use the height of the water, not the tank: 60 × 30 × 35 = 1800 × 35 = 63 000 cm³ = 63 L. 9 L is the empty space at the top.

items.q: A juice can is a cylinder with a radius of 3 cm and a height of 12 cm. About how many millilitres of juice does it hold? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: V = 3.14 × 3 × 3 × 12 = 28.26 × 12 = 339.12 cm³. 1 cm³ = 1 mL, so it holds about 339 mL. 1356 uses the diameter (6 cm) as r.

items.q: A water tank on a farm near Kamloops is a cylinder with a radius of 1 m and a height of 2 m. How many litres does it hold? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
A rain barrel in Vancouver is a cylinder with a diameter of 60 cm and a height of 90 cm. About how many litres of rain can it hold? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: r = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 cm. V = 3.14 × 30 × 30 × 90 = 2826 × 90 = 254 340 cm³ = 254 340 mL, which is about 254 L. 1017 L uses 60 cm as the radius.

items.q: A backyard pool in Kelowna is 8 m long and 4 m wide. The water is 1.5 m deep everywhere. How many litres of water are in the pool?
Hana builds a cedar planter box that is 120 cm long, 40 cm wide and 30 cm deep inside. Soil comes in 50 L bags. How many bags does she need to fill the box?
items.e: V = 120 × 40 × 30 = 144 000 cm³ = 144 L. 144 ÷ 50 = 2.88, so 2 bags are not enough. She needs 3 bags.

items.q: A juice box is 6 cm long, 4 cm wide and 10 cm high. How much juice can it hold?
items.e: V = 6 × 4 × 10 = 240 cm³. 1 cm³ = 1 mL, so it holds 240 mL. (2.4 L would be 2400 mL.)

items.q: Container A is a cylinder with a radius of 3 cm and a height of 10 cm. Container B is a box 7 cm × 7 cm × 6 cm. Which holds more, and by how much? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
A water cooler at the Terry Fox Run is a cylinder with a diameter of 40 cm and a height of 50 cm. How many litres does it hold? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
Sofia pours juice from a full 2 L jug into glasses. Each glass is a cylinder with a radius of 4 cm and a height of 10 cm. How many glasses can she fill all the way? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: One glass: 3.14 × 4 × 4 × 10 = 502.4 cm³ = 502.4 mL. 2 L = 2000 mL. 2000 ÷ 502.4 ≈ 3.98, so she can fill 3 glasses all the way (the 4th is not full).

items.q: An aquarium has a base 50 cm long and 25 cm wide. Ethan pours in 25 L of water. How deep is the water?
items.e: 25 L = 25 000 cm³. Base area: 50 × 25 = 1250 cm². Depth = 25 000 ÷ 1250 = 20 cm. 500 divides by the length only.

items.q: A rectangular water tank in an Okanagan orchard is 2 m long, 1.5 m wide and 1 m high. How many litres does it hold?
Owen takes a water bottle on a hike up the Grouse Grind. The bottle is a cylinder with a radius of 3.5 cm and a height of 20 cm. How much water does it hold? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
A storage bin holds 60 L. Its inside base is 50 cm long and 40 cm wide. How high is the inside of the bin?
items.e: 60 L = 60 000 cm³. Base area: 50 × 40 = 2000 cm². Height = 60 000 ÷ 2000 = 30 cm. 1200 divides by the length only.

items.q: A hose fills Liam’s 72 L fish tank at 4 L per minute. How many minutes does it take to fill the tank?
items.e: 72 ÷ 4 = 18 minutes. Check: 18 × 4 = 72 L. (288 multiplies, and 68 subtracts.)
